newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic /NYNEX termination fees set. [CORRECTED 18:43 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic /NYNEX termination fees set. [CORRECTED 18:43 GMT]

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp have set a minimum of $200 million in termination fees if their merger failed to be completed, and a maximum of $550 million, according to a proxy released on Monday.

Whichever party failed to complete the merger would pay the other the termination fee, which would rise to the maximum in case the failing party were acquired by or sold a subsidiary to another bidder within 18 months.
The document, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, says the new company -- Bell Atlantic -- has the authority to issue 2.5 billion shares of $0.10 nominal.
The board has the authority to issue 2.25 billion ordinary shares and 250 million preferred shares.
The new company will have 22 directors, 11 designated by NYNEX and 11 by Bell Atlantic.

The merger agreement includes Raymond Smith, chief executive of Bell Atlantic, retiring as chief executive of the new company two years after the completion of the deal, to be replaced by NYNEX's current chief executive Ivan Seidenberg.
The number of directors, prior to the retirment of Smith, can only be altered by the agreement of three quarters of the board. After his retirement a simple majority is enough.
The companies repeated the merger would cost $500 million in integration and transition charges in the first year and $200 million-$400 million in the succeeding two years.

But simultaneously-recurring savings of $300 million are targeted for the first year, rising to $600 million a year by year three. On top of this, $250 million to $300 million would be saved on capital spending each year on purchasing, market trials and equipment testing.
The company reiterated that cash flow margins should be stronger with the combined companies than either would be alone, and would add to earnings per share in the first year after the merger.
